messages:
alex: Customer on PROD getting intermittent 429s for some read endpoints. Org quota shows ~90% free but project quotas for proj-78 are at 0. Customer says they didn't hit project limits.
sara: Can you grab the raw request headers + gateway log lines for a failing request? Also confirm whether they're using API keys or OAuth.
alex: They use an API key in Authorization. Gateway log for a failing request:
<gateway-log> auth_method=api_key key_id=proj_78_key client_ip=34.201.10.22 x-forwarded-for=\"34.201.10.22,10.0.0.5\" quota_scope=project project_id=proj-78 decision=429 reason=quota_exhausted scope=project x-request-id=rqd-12345</gateway-log>
ops-bot: Alert: rate-limit-trigger project=proj-78 spike 429s @2026-03-15T14:03Z :warning:
mike: Hmm — gateway shows project scope which matches the project key, but weird that org quota looked healthy. Can you paste the curl you used to repro locally?
alex: Reproduced locally. If I include Authorization + X-Forwarded-For the request 429s. If I omit X-Forwarded-For it succeeds. Example:
```
# fails (returns 429)
curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer proj_78_key\" -H \"X-Forwarded-For: 34.201.10.22,10.0.0.5\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
# succeeds (200)
curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer proj_78_key\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
sara: :eyes: If true that suggests our router/quotas may be preferring IP-based attribution when XFF is present. API key should take precedence. @mike can you check quota-decider logic?
mike: On it. Quick hypothesis: our XFF parsing picks the first public IP (34.201.10.22) which maps via geo/ip->tenant table to a different org mapping, so the quota-decider falls back to IP scope. I'll reproduce against the quota service.
natalie: For immediate mitigation, ask the partner to stop rewriting X-Forwarded-For or to add X-Real-IP with the original client IP. We can also whitelist the NAT IP at the gateway to attribute to proj-78, or temporarily bump the project quota while we fix the routing logic.
alex: Customer requested a reproducible snippet to send to the partner. Added a POST example that also prints the relevant response headers:
```
curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -X POST \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer proj_78_key\" -H \"X-Forwarded-For: 34.201.10.22,10.0.0.5\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'
# response headers observed:
# x-rate-limit-scope: project
# x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
# x-request-id: rqd-12345
```
mike: Confirmed — reproed in staging. Found bug: precedence logic currently prefers IP mapping when XFF contains a public IP that matches a tenant-subnet entry. PR incoming to change precedence to prefer API key if present. Adding integration tests too.
sara: Great. Please add a regression test that simulates (API key + multi-value X-Forwarded-For) and asserts key-based attribution wins.
mike: Will do. Also putting a short-term gateway flag to prefer key-over-ip for requests from partner proxies while the code change lands.
alex: Customer notified; we applied a temporary project quota bump and asked their partner to stop rewriting XFF for the next 24h. They're validating now. I will close once they confirm :thumbsup:
